newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks storm ahead in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks storm ahead in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks soared into record territory in Wednesday morning trade, boosted by favourable trends surrounding the index's two biggest constituents and a strong inflow of hot money, brokers said.
"This is still a purely liquidity-driven market," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas. "All the speculative funds (in the region) are flowing to us."
The Hang Seng Index was trading 88 points higher at 14,620, after advancing nearly 130 points to a record high of 14,662.64 shortly after the opening bell. Turnover was robust at HK$2.51 billion.

Brokers said the index was boosted chiefly by a jump in Hong Kong Telecommunications, which added HK$0.65 to HK$17.45 in heavy trade of nearly HK$400 million. Investors believe the company was likely to see greater opportunities in China in future, brokers said.

HSBC Holdings was also strong, gaining HK$1.00 to HK$227.00. Clarification that the Hong Kong Monetary Authority was not seeking severe restrictions on banks' exposure to the property market boosted sentiment toward HSBC, a broker with large UK house said.
The index was also buoyed by Wall Street's second straight record close, brokers said.
The Dow closed 37.50 points higher at 7,383.41, boosted by gains in big blue chips and a buying spree in technology issues.
The May Hang Seng Index futures contract, which expires on Thursday, was trading a cautious 55 points higher at 14,625 at mid-morning.
